decisions.executionNote: Holder is in right workspace; orient right hand for a side grasp while leaving left arm clear. Start gently to preserve elbow-up continuity.
Rotate right gripper inward and approach holder gradually at its side, keeping the fingers open.
After continuity rejection, hold wrist orientation and use smaller translations toward the holder side.
Holder shifted during lateral approach. Retract fingers outward before realigning to avoid pushing it further.
Back away with a small wrist-yaw change to avoid the near-singular configuration; reassess the displaced holder.
Holder has fallen onto its side. Raise and reorient the right hand for a top-down recovery grasp, clear of the pens.
Reduce rotational and positional increments after the zero-step rejection; lift away while beginning the recovery orientation.
Continue above the fallen holder with clearance, turning the right fingers downward for a central grasp.
Align the downward right gripper across the fallen holder's middle. Keep clearance until wrist view confirms alignment.
Lower the open fingers around the holder's sides, keeping the downward grasp orientation fixed.
Close around the fallen holder, then lift a short distance to verify retention from the images.
Holder appears retained. Lift clear and begin rotating its long axis upright, keeping the right gripper closed.
Finish bringing the retained holder upright and position it near the center-right for insertion, without crossing arms.
Keep the holder upright in the right hand and make room beside its opening. Begin a gentle elbow-up left-hand approach toward the cyan pen.
Advance the left hand above the cyan pen while turning the fingers downward; right hand holds the holder stationary.
Center the left fingers above the cyan pen and finish the downward orientation before the final descent.
Descend onto the cyan pen and close the left gripper; keep the holder fixed and closed in the right hand.
Allow the left fingers to close at the observed contact height, then lift slightly to check cyan-pen retention.
Lift the retained cyan pen and turn it upright. Gently level and lower the held holder to improve insertion clearance.
Finish turning the cyan pen vertical above the holder. Keep both grips closed and verify mouth alignment before lowering.
Adjust cyan pen slightly left and forward, then lower its bottom into the visible opening while holding the cup steady.
Move the cyan pen farther toward the mouth center and slightly deeper, then release gently with the holder stationary.
The pen and holder tilted during release; resecure the cyan pen and lift it clear rather than forcing the rim.
Cyan is not retained in the left hand. Clear the left arm and lift/level the tilted holder before attempting another insertion.
Replan from the interrupted pose: raise and draw the right wrist back without further rotation to regain configuration margin.
Use a much smaller transition near the latest observed wrist pose, then cautiously lift and retreat to restore tracking margin.
With tracking restored, gently correct the holder's visible lean while lifting/backing the right wrist to preserve joint margin.
Bring the held holder nearer the shared working boundary and correct the remaining lean slowly; the cyan pen is visibly outside and needs recovery.
Correct the cup's fore-aft tilt based on the obscured opening, using small wrist changes and a little upward clearance.
Replan from the interrupted observation: smaller tilt increments with a short upward/backward retreat to reduce wrist tracking load.
Tilt the cup opening toward vertical in small increments. Move the clear left hand toward the purple pen, staying on its own side.
No motion executed on the rejected chunk. Reduce the left approach and pitch to small continuity-preserving steps; continue the cup correction cautiously.
Replan from current poses. Lower the held assembly toward a safer table-supported recovery while the left hand approaches the purple pen.
Unfold the right wrist away from its tracking limit while moving the holder toward table support. Continue a slow left approach above the purple pen.
Lower the held assembly toward the table without further twisting. Bring the left open fingers above the purple pen, turning downward during descent.
Finish aligning the left downward grasp over purple. Release the low, tilted holder onto the table for a clean recovery rather than force its current grip.
Back the left arm away from the rejected reach. Open the right grip at table height, then separate gently from the holder and cyan pen.
Clear the right hand from the released objects. Change the left wrist approach angle above purple to avoid the previous near-limit configuration.
Lower the left hand toward purple at the new grasp angle. Bring the right hand above the fallen holder with open fingers and clearance for a fresh grasp.
Make the final small purple alignment and close the left fingers. Align the right downward grasp across the holder's sides above the table.
Lift purple away from the table to verify retention. Finish centering the right downward fingers above the fallen holder before descending.
Lower and close the right fingers around the holder's middle. Lift and turn the retained purple pen away from the table, keeping both arms separated.
Lift the newly grasped holder straight clear before rotating it. Finish turning purple upward and keep it away from the holder during recovery.
Replan the left wrist with smaller rotation increments. Rotate the retained holder about its observed horizontal axis toward upright while keeping the purple pen clear.
Complete the holder's upright rotation and lower it to a comfortable insertion height. Approach with purple still above and to the left of the opening.
The holder is now upright. Lift purple clear of the rim and correct its visible lean before moving over the opening.
Translate purple over the mouth at constant height, preserving clearance before descent. Hold the right wrist still.
Lower purple toward the upright holder, correcting fore-aft alignment with the mouth center. Keep the cup completely still.
Lower purple a little farther through the centered opening, then open the left fingers without moving the holder.
Purple is visibly seated in the upright holder. Withdraw the left hand and turn toward a downward grasp on the yellow-ended pen.
Keep clear of the holder while completing most of the downward turn for the yellow-ended pen.
Center the downward left fingers across the yellow-ended pen, descending only to a clearance height before the final grasp.
Lower onto the yellow-ended pen and close the left fingers at its shaft. Keep the upright holder fixed.
Let the fingers finish closing, then lift the yellow-ended pen clear and away from the held cup to verify retention.
Yellow-ended pen is retained. Lift and turn it upright in free space, leaving the filled holder stationary.
Finish turning the retained yellow-ended pen upright and approach above the holder, leaving height for alignment.
Lift the long yellow-ended pen slightly and shift its lower end over the open side of the holder, avoiding the seated purple pen.
Correct the yellow pen's fore-aft lean while it remains above the cup, bringing its lower end toward the opening before descent.
Lower the yellow-ended pen toward the open right side of the holder, with small lateral correction and the cup held fixed.
Continue the slow vertical insertion of the yellow-ended pen into the clear side of the opening; keep both grips closed.
The yellow pen shifted as it entered. Release without further downward pressure, then lift the open left fingers to check whether it settles inside.
Yellow is visibly outside the cup. Lower the upright holder toward table support while clearing the left arm toward the black pen; preserve the seated purple pen.
Continue toward the black pen with a downward approach, and lower the held upright cup gently toward table support.
Align the left downward fingers around the black pen and descend to a near-grasp height. Hold the upright cup steady near the tabletop.
Make the final vertical descent around the black pen and close the left fingers without moving the cup.
Lift the black pen away from the table with the left fingers closed, checking retention before reorientation.
Black pen is visibly retained. Lift and rotate it toward vertical while moving through clear left-side space.
Finish orienting the black pen upright and move above the holder with its lower end still clear of the rim.
Use smaller wrist increments after the continuity rejection. Center the black pen above the holder and lower to a clearance height.
Correct the black pen slightly left and forward while lowering toward the mouth, keeping the upright cup fixed and avoiding the purple pen.
Lower the black pen through the visible opening a short distance, then release without further pressure while the right hand stabilizes the cup.
Black and purple are visibly seated. Clear the left fingers from them, then approach the cup's left side for a hand transfer so the right arm can collect the remaining right-side pens.
Lower the open left hand beside the holder, clear of the inserted pens, for a higher side grasp while the right hand continues supporting it.
Advance the open left fingers around the upper sides of the holder for the hand transfer, keeping the right support fixed.
Close the left fingers around the holder, pause for engagement, then open the right grip without translating either hand.
Separate the opened right hand, then lift and shift the holder slightly left to verify the new left-hand grip and clear the remaining pens.
Holder is retained by the left hand. Move it slightly left while replanning the right arm with a small upward/forward transition away from the continuity limit, beginning the cyan grasp orientation.
Turn the right fingers downward above the cyan pen with clearance; keep the left-held cup and its two seated pens stationary.
Center the right fingers above the cyan pen and finish the downward orientation, descending only to a clearance height.
Lower the centered right fingers onto the cyan pen and close gently, while the left hand keeps the holder upright.
Allow the right fingers to finish closing, then lift the cyan pen straight clear to verify retention before turning it.
